prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry holds thresholds/latency/connection protection/gate compatibility/towing priority/stand reopening/turnaround margins/materiality; in Adverse Weather/Capacity Reduction tightens escalation for near-departure flights, still suppresses low-impact local issues): Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction State(extended metering horizon); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit); Contingency Fallback(exception summaries via Contingency Operations Console, same role visibility); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Actors: Regional Flow Manager=RFM(ranks diversions; aggregated impact), Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, ADM(Medical Diversion Notice; publishes remote stand operating posture in Foxglove before first affected arrival bank), Ramp Control Lead(confirms each remote stand has aircraft route, safe passenger transfer path, blocked-apron contingency), Ground Handling Dispatcher=GHD(baggage reconciliation; Towbar Shortage Report; verifies bus assignments don't conflict with baggage/catering/fueling/crew transport on apron corridor), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(intent confirmation; uses remote stands for connections only if transfer time fits departure sequence), Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO, Data Governance Steward(limits exposed baggage/handler data to operational necessity). Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform. Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module; Arrival Regulation Console; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT, GDP, Pushback Window Token); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(Collaborative Decision Log); Common Situation Display; Emberline=Departure Metering Service(Registry threshold; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager; includes remote stand constraints in TOBT achievability); Ironleaf shall not advance aircraft unless remote stand release time supports taxi plan; Nightjar; Halcyon; Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Apron Sensors; Ramp Movement Board(stand exceptions; remote stand occupancy, towing, bus readiness); Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner(severity, duplicate suppression; produces Remote Stand Shuttle Count periodically); Performance Analytics Warehouse(compares escalations vs actual off-block to tune thresholds); Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Lantern; Alert

New part:
S554: If a bus shortage or terminal loading delay is detected, the Airline Operations Coordinator may request revision of the Target Off Block Time before the delay propagates to runway demand.
S555: The Regional Flow Manager considers repeated remote stand transfer delays as an input to tactical capacity assessment during peak arrival and departure banks.
S556: Ramp Control Lead uses the Towbar Shortage Report to determine whether remote stand aircraft can be repositioned without creating secondary apron congestion.
S557: The Capacity Assessment Module reflects persistent remote stand service limits as a reduction in practical gate throughput rather than only as a ramp movement issue.
S558: The Gate Conflict Detector identifies cases where an aircraft assigned to a contact gate would cause less overall delay than a nominally available remote stand with inadequate passenger transfer capacity.
S559: When remote stand use increases, the Airport CDM Portal records the operational reason, affected flights, expected passenger transfer duration, and responsible control position.
S560: The Common Situation Display presents remote stand status in time order so that airline, ramp, tower, and airport roles share the same expectation for aircraft readiness.
S561: Landside service limits are linked to airside timing through estimated boarding completion, bus return availability, crew access, and terminal processing constraints.
S562: A remote stand departure is not considered ready for push or tow until passengers, bags, crew, and required ground services are aligned with the planned aircraft movement.
S563: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Airport Duty Manager may reduce planned remote stand use because bus loading, walking routes, and accessible transfer times become less predictable.
S564: During Recovery Phase, remote stands may be used to absorb late arrivals while preserving contact gates for flights with tight turnarounds or high connection sensitivity.
S565: The Performance Analytics Warehouse retains remote stand timing measures so that planners can compare scheduled assumptions with actual passenger transfer and apron release performance.
S566: This section extends the remote stand performance concept by describing how border, customs, and apron sensing inputs become constraints in the daily operating plan.
S567: Border release status is represented as a readiness attribute on each affected flight record in the Regional Flow Platform, separate from aircraft readiness and airline commercial readiness.
S568: The Airport Duty Manager produces the Customs Hold Release Note when border processing confirms that a held arrival may proceed to normal turnaround handling.
S569: Customs hold indicators are represented as operational constraints that prevent premature stand release, passenger transfer assumptions, or departure readiness claims.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
